mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 5.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative following two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their previous month's values indicates a soft labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both increase month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both HOUST and GDPC1 signals a housing market downturn coinciding with broader demand weakness, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and GDPC1 decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent CPIAUCSL above 2.5% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which increases the likelihood of aggressive central bank tightening and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of CPIAUCSL > 2.5% for six months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real personal savings (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as elevated savings buffer consumer spending uncertainty and support market optimism.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS increases month-over-month.
